explanation: Bananas are famous for their potassium, but weight for weight avocados, raw spinach and potatoes all hold more of it.

claims.text: Raw avocado contains about 485 mg of potassium per 100 g.
Raw banana contains about 358 mg of potassium per 100 g.
Raw spinach and raw potatoes also contain more potassium per 100 g than bananas.

issues.note: 'An avocado' is generic. I recall the USDA listing larger, watery Florida-type avocados at roughly the banana's figure, so the margin of 485 against 358 holds for Hass-type and all-variety averages but not for every avocado.

The explanation says 'potatoes' without 'raw' (only spinach carries it in the sentence). Raw or baked potato beats the banana, but by my recollection of the USDA table a boiled, peeled potato falls just below it, so 'raw potatoes' would be safer.
